candidates.name: OpenClaw

discoverySources.query: Inspect the pinned project naming history for OpenClaw and its former product names.
discoverySources.evidence: The pinned project documentation records the naming sequence Warelay, Clawdbot, Moltbot, and OpenClaw.

discoverySources.query: Inspect the historical in-process Pi SDK integration documentation.
discoverySources.evidence: The pinned document describes direct integration of pi-coding-agent, pi-ai, pi-agent-core, and pi-tui through AgentSession APIs.

discoverySources.query: Inspect the pre-cutoff provenance notice for retained Pi lineage.
discoverySources.evidence: The notice records portions of OpenClaw adapted from Pi/pi-mono and a retained @earendil-works/pi-tui dependency.

discoverySources.query: Inspect the runtime migration commit that introduced the OpenClaw-owned agent core and removed the former embedded Pi runtime layout.
discoverySources.evidence: The migration commit records extraction of an OpenClaw-owned agent-core package, removal of Pi runtime internals, and preservation of third-party provenance for incorporated code.

discoverySources.query: Inspect the pinned root package identity and retained Pi TUI dependency.
discoverySources.evidence: The pinned root manifest uses the openclaw npm identity and retains @earendil-works/pi-tui at 0.82.1.

candidates.dispositionReason: Phase-1 gap lead queued for the normal source-review gate; current scope, compatibility, risk, tests, maintenance, and license evidence remain unassessed.
candidates.evidenceSummary: OpenClaw historically embedded the Pi coding-agent, AI, agent-core, and TUI packages directly. It later internalized the Pi-shaped runtime as OpenClaw-owned agent core while retaining explicit Pi provenance and, at the pinned pre-cutoff state, a pi-tui dependency. This records historical and derived lineage only; it makes no current Pi v0.83 compatibility conclusion.

candidates.name: oh-my-pi

discoverySources.query: Inspect the pinned README for the declared Pi fork lineage and the fork's own product surfaces.
discoverySources.evidence: The pinned README identifies the project as a fork of Pi and describes its own terminal, SDK, RPC, and native ACP surfaces, including the explicit statement that ACP uses no bridge.

discoverySources.query: Inspect the pinned coding-agent manifest for the candidate-owned package identity.
discoverySources.evidence: The pinned manifest publishes @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent from this fork and depends on the fork's @oh-my-pi package family.

candidates.dispositionReason: Phase-1 gap lead queued for the normal source-review gate; inherited and independent behavior, compatibility, risk, tests, maintenance, and license evidence remain unassessed.
candidates.evidenceSummary: Pinned pre-cutoff material identifies a fork of Pi that publishes its own runtime, terminal UI, SDK, RPC, and native ACP surfaces. These are surfaces provided by the fork, not evidence that it consumes upstream Pi through SDK, RPC, or ACP. The boundary between inherited behavior and independent implementation still requires item-level review.
